column1: # JEPA hyperparameter sweep. One config per line: <name> TAB <args for train_jepa.py>.
# The array task id indexes the non-comment lines, so keep them stable while a
# sweep is in flight -- reordering renames every run's output directory.
# Short runs on purpose. The question here is which direction is worth a long
# run, not what the final number is; the winner gets retrained before it is
# reported. Everything varies against `base`, one axis at a time, so a result
# can be attributed to the axis rather than to a combination.
# The masking ratios are the JEPA-specific knob and get four lines: how much of
# the volume is hidden, and whether it is hidden across space or across time.
# That choice decides what the predictor has to model -- spatial masking asks it
# to complete an eyeball from its surroundings, temporal masking asks it to
# extrapolate motion, which is closer to what gaze decoding needs.
base
lr-high
lr-low
wide
small
mask-heavy
mask-light
mask-temporal
mask-spatial
window-50
# window-200 at batch 32 is an OOM on a 64 GB A100 and is kept here only so the
# line numbering does not move. Attention is quadratic in token count: the
# patcher makes 72 spatial x (window/5) temporal tokens, so 1440 tokens at
# window 100 becomes 2880 at window 200 and the attention weights alone want
# ~8 GB per layer. Rerun it at batch 8, with a batch-8 window-100 control, or
# the window axis is confounded with the batch axis.
window-200
batch-64
wd-high
